questions.q: In MVC, which part is responsible for connecting user actions to data and deciding what happens next?
questions.explanation: The Controller is the mediator in MVC: it receives a user action (from the View), queries or updates data (via the Model), then decides what to display next. The Model holds data logic; the View just renders what it's given.

questions.q: What core assumption does Agile make that Waterfall does not?
choices: Requirements will change during development, and the process should expect that
Testing should never happen until the very end
Developers should never talk to stakeholders
All requirements must be finalized before coding begins
questions.explanation: Agile's defining assumption is that requirements will change — often because users don't fully know what they want until they see early versions. Waterfall assumes requirements can be fully defined upfront, which rarely holds in practice.

questions.q: What's the core idea behind component-based frontend architecture?
choices: The UI is broken into small, self-contained, reusable pieces that manage their own state
All application logic must live in one controller file
Components replace the need for a backend entirely
Each component connects directly to the database
questions.explanation: Component-based architecture breaks the UI into small, self-contained pieces — each owning its own template, styles, and behavior — composed together the way HTML is assembled from elements. React, Vue, and Alpine all use this model.
